answer: Reputation should be earned, not claimed: require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can vouch for others, with the stake slashed when a vouched identity is later proven fake. A lone actor spinning up a nebula of sock-puppets must fund every one, so attack cost scales linearly while honest participation stays cheap. The old fable that identity is free dies once sybils carry a price: even a jade-perfect forgery cannot fake a funded, time-aged stake, and slashing makes coordinated fraud unprofitable before it can distort the ledger.
